chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Jafar Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sad b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Ali b. al-Numan from Abdullah b. Talha from al-Sadiq Jafar b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:
The fasting person is in the worship of Allah, even when he is sleeping on his bed, as long as he does not backbite a Muslim.

key_terms.الصائم: The fasting person (al-sa'im), one observing the fast
key_terms.يغتب: Backbiting (ightiyab), speaking ill of someone in their absence

ai.seo_question: Is a fasting person considered to be in worship even while sleeping?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (s) teaches that a fasting person remains in a state of worship even while asleep, with the sole condition being that they refrain from backbiting. This hadith, narrated through the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt, elevates the spiritual status of fasting beyond mere abstinence from food, emphasizing that the entire state of fasting is worship, but backbiting nullifies this elevated status.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from `Ali b. al-Nu`man from `Abdullah b. Talha from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
The fasting person is in the worship of Allah, even when he is sleeping on his bed; as long as he is not backbiting a Muslim.
